title: libdvdcss2 removed by MakeMKV layer autoremove — DVDs can't decrypt (CSS)
description: The MakeMKV build layer in the Dockerfile ends with 'apt-get autoremove -y', which removes libdvdcss2 (and libdvd-pkg) as orphans since HandBrake dlopens libdvdcss at runtime (no hard dpkg dependency). Result: CSS-encrypted DVDs can't be decrypted — HandBrake enumerates titles via libdvdnav but prints 'Encrypted DVD support unavailable / No css library available', and /api/scan returns 0 usable titles; rips would fail. Regression introduced with the Blu-ray feature (the makemkv layer). Pre-Blu-ray image had libdvdcss (user ripped 8 DVDs). Fix: apt-mark manual libdvdcss2 libdvd-pkg before the autoremove (keep them), rebuild, verify libdvdcss present + DVD scan returns titles.
close_reason: Fixed: libdvdcss now built in a dedicated Dockerfile layer after the makemkv autoremove. Verified on real hardware — libdvdcss2 1.4.3 installed, DVD scan returns 27 titles (was 0), main feature detected.

title: Blu-ray output: use MKV container (soft PGS subs + lossless audio)
description: Blu-ray rips should output .mkv instead of .mp4 so the disc's PGS subtitle tracks embed as soft/selectable (MP4 can't carry PGS) and lossless audio can pass through. DVD stays .mp4. Plex Direct Plays/Direct Streams MKV H.264; burning bitmap subs on a client still transcodes (accepted tradeoff). Changes: path extension by disc_format, HandBrake --format av_mkv + drop --optimize for MKV, keep soft subtitle embed. Resolves the PGS-in-MP4 limitation.
close_reason: Done: BD outputs .mkv; verified the soft PGS English subtitle survives in the output (HandBrake scan). 88 tests pass.

title: Blu-ray: PGS subtitles can't be soft-embedded in MP4 (only burned)
description: Blu-ray subtitles are PGS (bitmap). MP4 cannot carry PGS as a soft/selectable track (unlike DVD VOBSUB, which HandBrake muxes fine). In the shakedown, requesting subtitle 1 (English) with burn_forced=false produced an MP4 with ZERO subtitle tracks — HandBrake silently dropped the PGS sub. This conflicts with the user's subtitle preference (embed disc English soft + burn forced). Options: (a) burn English subs into the picture (always-on, not selectable); (b) output MKV for Blu-ray (carries PGS soft + lossless audio; Plex plays MKV but Chromecast may transcode); (c) only burn forced subs on BD, no soft English; (d) OCR PGS->SRT (needs extra tooling). NEEDS USER DECISION.
notes: Forced-sub burn (HandBrake Foreign Audio Search) DOES work for PGS; only the soft/selectable embed fails for MP4.
close_reason: Resolved by dvd-rip-p42: Blu-ray now outputs MKV, which carries PGS as a soft/selectable track. Verified on a real rip.

title: Container: work around makemkv.com DNSSEC SERVFAIL with static hosts entry
description: makemkv.com authoritative DNS is returning SERVFAIL under DNSSEC validation (dig +cd resolves to 88.212.208.67; all validating resolvers fail). makemkvcon's HTTP license/online check then can't resolve the host and the disc scan hangs (99% CPU, no output) — previously misdiagnosed as 'host lost internet'. Add an extra_hosts entry in docker-compose.yml mapping makemkv.com + www.makemkv.com to the +cd-resolved IP so the container bypasses the broken DNSSEC. Port 80 (HTTP) on that IP serves 200; port 443 is closed (MakeMKV check is HTTP). Temporary: remove/refresh once MakeMKV fixes their DNSSEC.
notes: RESOLVED root cause: the hang was NOT (only) DNS. makemkvcon hung at 100% CPU in 'SDF auto' drive-firmware processing for the non-LibreDrive Pioneer BDR-XD08 (known MakeMKV bug on Linux). Fix = sdf_Stop setting (via MAKEMKV_SDF_STOP env -> entrypoint writes it) to run standard AACS mode (fine for 1080p). Also added app_UpdateEnable=0 so makemkvcon never phones home. makemkv.com's DOMAIN REGISTRATION LAPSED (DNSSEC SERVFAIL; only registrar parking page on :80, :443 refused) — that's why SDF/SVQ auto-download can't work; extra_hosts pins a reachable IP so stray lookups fail fast instead of hanging. Scan validated: 11 titles, title 2=main (2:21:37), parser matches real output (new fixture+test). decrypt_title also fixed for stale-MKV overwrite false-negative.
close_reason: Resolved: real cause was the MakeMKV SDF 100%-CPU hang on the non-LibreDrive Pioneer drive, fixed via sdf_Stop + app_UpdateEnable=0 (entrypoint from MAKEMKV_SDF_STOP). extra_hosts kept as DNS-failfast belt-and-suspenders. Full BD+ scan->decrypt->encode validated on The Martian.

title: Surface HandBrake error output on job failure

Fix: collect the last ~25 non-progress output lines in a ring buffer and append them to the FAILED job's error field for diagnosability. Also bump chunk read 256->4096 to cut syscall rate.

Update test_presets.py assertions.

title: _cleanup_partial: unlink on cancel/fail unconditionally

title: Progress bar stuck at 0% during rip
description: Job runs and output file grows, but UI shows 0%. Cause: HandBrakeCLI emits the 'Encoding: task X of Y, P.PP %' progress lines terminated with \r (carriage return) so they overwrite themselves in a terminal. proc.stdout.readline() blocks waiting for \n, never returning during encoding. Fix: read raw chunks and split on either \r or \n.

title: Eject fails with 'device busy' when host auto-mounts disc
description: User reports clicking Eject in UI fails with 'eject failed: device /dev/sr0 busy', but physical eject button works. Cause: GNOME/udisks2 auto-mounts the DVD on the host when inserted; the container's eject tries the kernel eject ioctl which fails with EBUSY because the host has the device mounted. Fix: fall back to 'eject -s' (SCSI direct command) which tells the drive's firmware to open the tray regardless of mount state (equivalent to the physical button).

title: Scan: probe DVD-Video with lsdvd before running makemkvcon
description: Since the Blu-ray feature, /api/scan always runs 'makemkvcon info' first as the disc-type detector, then falls back to the DVD scanner when it's not a Blu-ray. So every DVD scan pays a slow, pointless makemkvcon analysis pass (CSS DVD that MakeMKV will never rip) before the real HandBrake/lsdvd scan — noticeably sluggish 'weird' behaviour. Fix: add a cheap is_dvd_video(device) probe (lsdvd: reads only VIDEO_TS, fast, fails fast on BD) and only invoke makemkvcon when the disc is NOT a DVD. DVD scans skip makemkvcon entirely; Blu-ray auto-detect preserved.

title: Blu-ray track selection: info-scan indices may not map 1:1 to extracted MKV
description: For Blu-ray, the UI lists tracks from 'makemkvcon info' (e.g. The Martian title 3 = 1 audio + 10 subs), but MakeMKV's default profile saves a SUBSET into the MKV (that title's MKV had 1 audio + 5 subs). HandBrake then encodes the MKV using selection indices that came from the info scan, so high/non-English subtitle or audio indices can point at the wrong stream or a missing one. The common case (English audio + English/forced subs = index 1) aligns correctly because MakeMKV orders the primary tracks first. Fix options: (a) parse the MKV's actual streams post-decrypt and remap, (b) drive MakeMKV's track selection so the MKV matches the scan, or (c) constrain the BD UI to MKV-available tracks. Until then, non-default BD track picks are best-effort.
notes: Discovered during BD shakedown 2026-06-16. HandBrake ignores out-of-range subtitle indices, so a default rip still produces a valid MP4.
close_reason: Won't affect real usage: user only ever selects English subtitles, which are the primary track (index 1) and map correctly between the info scan and the extracted MKV. The 1:1 divergence only manifests for non-English/high-index picks, which won't happen. Reasoning preserved here if usage ever changes.

(2) parse_handbrake_scan: wrap json.loads in try/except JSONDecodeError to avoid a 500 on truncated scan output. (3) subscriber asyncio.Queue is unbounded; add maxsize or latest-value pattern. (4) _cleanup_partial swallows OSError silently; log it.

title: Secure remote access: control rips from outside the LAN
description: Allow triggering/monitoring rips from outside the home network (start scans/rips, watch progress, browse library). Physical constraint: a disc must still be loaded in the drive at home — remote access only controls the rip, it can't insert media. BLOCKER for any exposure: the app currently has NO authentication and binds 0.0.0.0:8000 (already LAN-reachable), so it must never be port-forwarded raw to the internet — anyone reaching it could scan/rip/cancel/browse and spawn HandBrake/makemkvcon jobs. Options to evaluate: (1) VPN overlay (Tailscale/WireGuard) — simplest + safest, nothing exposed publicly (recommended default); (2) add app-level auth (HTTP basic or an auth layer) + TLS reverse proxy (Caddy/nginx) if public exposure is required. Decide approach before implementing; lean VPN.
notes: Raised 2026-06-17. Confirmed no auth/middleware on any endpoint; subprocess calls are argv-based (no shell-injection) but endpoints are unprotected.

value: Never run 'make restart', 'make down', or 'make build && make restart' in this project while a HandBrake job is running/queued — it kills the worker and leaves a partial MP4 in OUTPUT_DIR. Always check curl http://localhost:8000/api/jobs first; if status=running or queued, ask the user before proceeding. The Makefile 'check-no-active-jobs' target enforces this with FORCE=1 override.

Blu-ray feature: COMPLETE + fully validated on real hardware (The Martian BD+, Pioneer BDR-XD08), branch feat/bluray-support, NOT yet merged to main. Pipeline proven end-to-end via /api/rip: scan -> decrypt(makemkvcon) -> HandBrake NVENC encode -> playable .MKV with soft/selectable English PGS subtitle + AAC + AC3, host-owned perms, library records disc_format=bluray. KEY DECISIONS/FIXES: (1) makemkvcon SDF hang on non-LibreDrive drive fixed via sdf_Stop (MAKEMKV_SDF_STOP env -> entrypoint) = standard AACS mode (fine for 1080p) + app_UpdateEnable=0 (no phone-home); makemkv.com domain lapsed so generic SVQ used for BD+. (2) BLU-RAY OUTPUTS .MKV not .mp4 (user chose this) because MP4 can't carry PGS bitmap subs as soft tracks; DVD stays .mp4; container derived from output extension in build_handbrake_args (av_mkv, no --optimize). Other fixes: scan timeout 180->600s, decrypt_title stale-MKV overwrite false-negative, library disc_format never persisted (+migration). 88 tests pass. Remaining: dvd-rip-2bx epic open (close on merge), dvd-rip-dip P2 (non-default BD track selection indices don't map 1:1 to extracted MKV; English index 1 is fine). A full 2h21m movie rip not yet run (only short extras) but pipeline identical. .env has MAKEMKV_SDF_STOP=PIONEER_BD-RW___BDR-XD08_1.00_BHDL000771UC.

Dockerfile gotcha (dvd-rip): NEVER run 'apt-get autoremove' after libdvdcss2 is built. HandBrake dlopens libdvdcss at runtime, so no package declares a hard dpkg dependency on it — autoremove judges it an unused orphan and silently removes it, breaking ALL CSS-DVD decryption (HandBrake then enumerates titles via libdvdnav but returns 0 usable ones: 'Encrypted DVD support unavailable / No css library available'; rips fail). This rode in with the Blu-ray feature's makemkv build layer (which purges build-essential + autoremoves). Fix in place: libdvd-pkg is installed/built in its OWN dedicated Dockerfile layer AFTER the makemkv layer's autoremove. Verify after any Docker change: 'docker run --rm --entrypoint sh dvd-rip-dvd-rip -c "ldconfig -p | grep dvdcss"' must show libdvdcss.so.2. Symptom on hardware: /api/scan returns 0 titles for a DVD even though lsdvd lists them.

UI preferences for dvd-rip project: (1) clean/utility design, NOT decorated (user pushed back on eyebrow labels, brand marks, italic flourishes, grain textures, colophons as 'trying too hard to be fancy'); (2) cool blue-gray palette over warm/brown (panels #161922, body #0c0e13, text #e1e5ed); (3) Prussian Ink accent #4b73b8 — muted blue, not bright; (4) IBM Plex Sans/Mono only (no Fraunces or other display serifs). When iterating: keep typography distinctive but restrained, accent used sparingly on functional elements only (toggles, progress, focus rings).

Subtitle preference for dvd-rip: use the DISC's own subtitle tracks, NOT Plex's downloaded/text subtitles (user has had accuracy problems with Plex-downloaded subs). Embed the disc's English subtitle track (soft/selectable) + burn forced subs from the disc. Accept that disc subs are bitmap (DVD VOBSUB / Blu-ray PGS) so enabling them on Chromecast triggers a Plex burn-transcode — accuracy is worth it. USER ONLY EVER USES ENGLISH SUBTITLES — never selects another language. Implication: the track-index mapping caveat for non-English/high-index picks (was dvd-rip-dip) does NOT affect real usage, since English is the primary track (index 1) which maps correctly between the makemkvcon scan and the extracted MKV. Blu-ray outputs MKV (not MP4) so the English PGS sub stays soft/selectable.
